records.alternative_mechanism: Different admissible command and contact histories can produce the same selected endpoint observable. Matching speed alone does not match the full terminal state or internal history.
records.critique_question: Does selecting only endpoint speed make distinct internal mechanisms appear equivalent by construction?
records.discriminating_measurement: Declare the endpoint map, event and matching tolerance; compare full state, work, loads, constraints and robustness among matched outcomes. Separately test model interventions from the same complete dynamical state.
records.title: Similar Endpoints Can Hide Different Internal Pathways

records.alternative_mechanism: Continuing a specified command channel can change both timing and the delivery objective. That conditional intervention effect does not identify a universal benefit of the observed sequence.
records.critique_question: Is an observed timing change being treated as beneficial without a matched objective and intervention?
records.discriminating_measurement: Branch the registered model at the same event and complete state, including any activation or compliance states. Declare the command-removal operation, other command histories or feedback policies, endpoint rule and uncertainty; compare objective, work and loads together.
records.title: A Timing Change Is Not Automatically Beneficial Transfer

records.alternative_mechanism: Coordinate partitions and unweighted least-squares metrics can change attributed components and the fitted force. The reconstructed generalized drive includes the retained residual; a force-only fit need not identify the complete physical wrench.
records.critique_question: Does a named generalized component survive a change of coordinates and physical endpoint representation?
records.discriminating_measurement: Transform the same physical trajectory, generalized covectors, Jacobian and residual metric consistently. Check total virtual power and reconstruction in one observer frame; report rank, residual and fitted-force sensitivity separately. Do not demand invariance of arbitrary component allocations.
records.title: Attribution Depends on Coordinates and Endpoint Mapping

records.alternative_mechanism: Equal-and-opposite force increments preserve resultant force but generally change its moment. Increments along the line joining ideal point contacts can preserve the complete wrench while changing individual contact loads, subject to admissibility constraints.
records.critique_question: Is a net club wrench being used to infer individual-hand loading, effort, or muscle coordination?
records.discriminating_measurement: Express synchronized bilateral force-and-moment measurements about one reference point and frame, with calibration and uncertainty. Check net-wrench closure and admissible nullspace changes. These measurements constrain contact allocation, not unique muscle effort or co-contraction.
records.title: One Net Club Wrench Does Not Identify Two Hand Loads

records.alternative_mechanism: A fixed ideal support can exchange momentum while doing zero work at its stationary contact. A prescribed moving base can supply or remove mechanical energy. A finite-mass dynamic base changes the coupled response; none of these facts alone disproves a late negative couple.
records.critique_question: Would the apparent mechanism persist when base motion is endogenous rather than prescribed or fixed?
records.discriminating_measurement: Map compatible physical initial states and event rules across fixed, prescribed and dynamic-base models. Include support reactions and prescribed-base power in the chosen system boundary; test sign, reconstruction, convergence and geometry controls without treating unlike models as the same experiment.
records.title: Base Constraints Change the Modeled Coupling

records.alternative_mechanism: Shaft deformation stores energy, but the sign and timing of its release, damping, contact and continuing actuation determine delivery. Equal peak deformation does not specify endpoint speed or an energetic benefit.
records.critique_question: Is peak shaft strain being credited as beneficial recoil without matching actuation, damping, contact, and endpoint?
records.discriminating_measurement: Declare either a fixed-command comparison of endpoint outcomes or a matched-delivery comparison of required inputs and losses. Keep the endpoint definition and event rule fixed, account for changed inertia and contact, and measure deformation and boundary power. Do not silently impose both identical commands and identical outcomes.
records.title: Shaft Recoil, Actuation, Damping, and Contact Are Confounded
